summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, bladder and prostate cancer status post cystectomy with ileal conduit, and chronic substance use was admitted for altered mental status and reported hematemesis. He was found with a colostomy bag off and reported multiple falls, though imaging showed no acute intracranial abnormalities. Urine toxicology was positive for oxycodone and opiates, indicating intoxication as the likely cause of altered mental status. His hemoglobin dropped from 9.7 to 8.4 g/dL during the admission, reflecting worsening anemia. A chest X-ray showed mild pulmonary congestion and bibasilar opacities. Urine culture grew E. coli and Enterococcus, but due to chronic colonization from urinary diversions, antibiotics were withheld. The patient left against medical advice on the second hospital day after being counseled on the risks, including potential death from ongoing substance use and severe anemia. He was advised to continue home medications and follow up with his primary care provider.
